name: Guyana

facts.religion: Christian about 63%, Hindu about 25%, Muslim about 7%

system_note: The executive president is chosen through party list voting.
snapshot: An oil boom has made Guyana's economy the world's fastest-growing, and Irfaan Ali won a second term in 2025 promising to share the wealth, while Venezuela claims two-thirds of its land.
culture: Guyana is South America's only English-speaking country and culturally Caribbean, with Indo-Guyanese and Afro-Guyanese communities, plus Amerindian peoples, Chinese and Portuguese. Phagwah (Holi), Diwali, Eid and Mashramani, the republic day carnival, are all national holidays. Kaieteur Falls, one of the world's highest single-drop waterfalls, lies in pristine rainforest.
society: ExxonMobil's offshore discoveries since 2015 turned a poor country into a petro-state, with GDP growth above 30 percent some years. Politics has long split along ethnic lines between the PPP, backed mainly by Indo-Guyanese, and the PNC. Venezuela claims the Essequibo region and held a referendum in 2023 on annexing it.
situation: Irfaan Ali's People's Progressive Party won the September 2025 election, and a new party led by Azruddin Mohamed, a businessman sanctioned by the US, came second, displacing the PNC-led opposition. Ali has pledged to spend oil revenue on housing, health and cash grants. Even with Maduro gone from Caracas, the government says Venezuela's claim to the Essequibo region remains a threat.
power: A presidential republic in which the leader of the winning party list becomes executive president for five years, at most two terms, and appoints a prime minister from parliament.

sources.label: AFP via NAMPA: Guyana wary of Venezuela
